prompt: After publishing a CSS fix, some visitors go on seeing the old version for hours. The site is behind a CDN. What is the structural solution?
hint: There is the usual way out — asking the CDN to forget what it kept. And there is another, which makes the problem stop happening. What stops two different versions from competing for the same name?

choices.text: Give the file a name fingerprinted from its content, so that any change changes the name and the HTML points at a different address.
choices.why: It is the same solution as the cache lesson, now at world scale: different names never compete for the same cache.

choices.text: Reduce `max-age` to a few seconds on every static file.
choices.why: It works, but throws away the CDN's benefit — the file gets fetched again all the time.

choices.text: Turn the CDN off for the stylesheets and always serve them from the origin.
choices.why: It cures the symptom by giving up exactly the content that benefits most from the CDN.

choices.text: Send `no-store` on the HTML, which makes the CDN re-evaluate the files it references too.
choices.why: The directive applies to the document itself; it does not reach the files referenced by it.

prompt: A shop with steady traffic all year round is migrating away from shared hosting. Tick the statements that hold up.
hint: Two of the options sell elasticity to someone with no variation to stretch. And remember that the cost of a VPS is not only the invoice.

choices.text: A VPS transfers responsibility for updates, backups and the firewall to the shop.
choices.why: That is what really changes in the migration — not the power, but whose responsibility it is.

choices.text: The cloud's elasticity pays off little here, because there is no varying demand to follow.
choices.why: Elasticity pays off when demand varies; with steady traffic it usually costs more than a VPS.

choices.text: A CDN helps even without changing hosting, because it sits in front of it.
choices.why: The CDN does not replace the origin: it precedes it, and takes care of what is static.

choices.text: The cloud eliminates the noisy neighbour because resources are no longer shared.
choices.why: Shared instances still exist in the cloud; what changes is the isolation you pay for, not the absence of neighbours.

choices.text: Migrating to a VPS lowers the total cost, since the monthly invoice tends to be similar.
choices.why: The invoice is similar; the total cost rises in administration hours, which is where the sum really changes.
